review.evidence: Ethereum block 26197387, hash 0x530cc1059f89d04e8a499a738ba8a4983a6a5695ffe0fa29d5bd25934b8dd702, timestamp 2026-10-15T10:42:35.000Z. Reconciled complete Ethereum and four L2 native vault authorization-event censuses with pinned getters. Ethereum retains its identified Spark/Chief/DSPause execution chain and observed 172800-second scheduling delay. Each L2 vault has its official Spark executor as the sole active event-enumerated ward, with the executor self-administered, one official Spark receiver holding SUBMISSION_ROLE, and local delay()=0. Local receipt issuance remains deposit-backed. This closes the omitted L2 controller inventory; it does not certify complete upstream message authentication, human-control independence, non-exportable signing keys or immutable scheduling. Native controls belong here; upstream bridged sUSDS controls remain on that linked asset. Spark family harmonization retains scoreable disposition: SubProxy and Executor delegatecalls write their own controller storage, and exhaustive historical delegated-write closure is not a new gate for legacy-equivalent controls. Unlike immutable MetaMorpho/VaultV2 siblings, these Legacy UsdcVault proxies positively expose authorized upgrade reach; every Ethereum/L2 proxy-admin control remains upgrade-only and can replace share logic. No favorable execution-scope narrowing, execution-complete certificate or immutable scheduling bound is claimed. Ethereum SubProxy remains dao-governor with observed 172800-second delay; the separate Base Executor remains contract with zero additional local delay.
